clue.text: OT turned into a musical, sadly disastrous

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written: the Old Testament abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone has turned the Old Testament into a stage musical, with dire results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned into' looks like the anagram signal but is only a link; 'sadly' rearranges OT + A + MUSICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calamitous brings calamity, so it is a synonym for catastrophic.

clue.text: Confer with first warrant officer after promotion

parts.note: first, as in first-rate or best in class, gives best

indicators.note: in a down clue promotion moves letters upward, so the abbreviation is read bottom to top after the first piece

explanation.surface: An officer is to be consulted on the matter of his own promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after promotion' works twice: the officer comes after 'first', and in a down clue promotion means moving up, so WO reads upwards as OW.
explanation.definitionFit: To confer an honour is to grant or present it, which is exactly the verb's meaning.

parts.note: a chord is a group of musical notes; playing its notes one after another rather than together breaks it up

explanation.surface: A famous band has split up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted group' sounds like a celebrated band, but means a group of written musical notes, a chord, played spread out.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken chord, its notes sounded in succession, is the musical term described.

indicators.note: consumed in says the numeral is swallowed inside the word for a jet

parts.note: spirt is a variant spelling of spurt, a jet of liquid
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone downs a drink while flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' suggests an aircraft, but it is a jet of liquid, SPIRT (an old spelling of spurt), which takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky, gin and other liquors are spirits, so a spirit is a strong alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: cowhand, not acceptable without subtle zap

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'cowhand, not acceptable without subtle zap', begins in lower case and has no definition: the opening word(s) defining the soup are missing, and 'subtle' has no job in GA(ZAP)CHO; no scan, and a search of the exact text found nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: cowhand, not acceptable without subtle zap

indicators.note: eschewed means avoided or given up, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: plush means luxurious or elegant
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: King Henry turned down a fine possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a king, but is the physics unit whose symbol is H, dropped from PLUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or benefit, the same sense as an asset to a team.

clue.text: Service returned with energy and go

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the service's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A church service is back on, full of vigour and drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a church or tennis, but is the Royal Air Force, whose letters turned give FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To fare is to get on or progress, as in 'how did you go?', so the verbs match.

indicators.note: hazardous implies danger and chance, so the letters are scattered at random

explanation.surface: Crete is described as a dangerous spot to send a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks like a ship to go with Crete, but means a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A container such as a bowl or bin is a vessel in the holding-things sense.

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter here

explanation.surface: A dead performer is eulogised in song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges SUNG + LATE + ACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To congratulate someone is to commend them warmly, a form of praising.

clue.text: Deities — one of them with a male name

parts.note: Pan, the Greek god of the wild, is one of the deities
Theon is a man's name, as in Theon of Alexandria

explanation.surface: Among the gods, one carries a man's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' points back to the definition: one of the deities is PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is the whole set of gods of a people, so it names the collective deities.

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the rest means the others
governor is slang for father, hence pa

explanation.surface: Other people are eating the governor's evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'governor' suggests an official, but is old slang for one's father, PA. The question mark flags dinner as just one example of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, of which dinner is one example.

parts.note: grand means big
a wig is worn on the head

explanation.surface: An important person wears an impressive hairpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig is an important person, the slang equivalent of a very important person.

clue.text: Name about to be stuck in guide's net-bag

indicators.note: stuck in means placed inside, so the reversed word goes into the guide

parts.note: a rule is a guide or principle

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for naming is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: Someone's name is about to be put into a guidebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it means 'nearly', but it turns the naming word round; 'to be stuck in' then puts that inside the guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticule is a small drawstring handbag, originally of netting, carried by women.

clue.text: Female garment displays a meadow flower

parts.note: a female's belongs to a lady, giving lady's
a smock is a loose garment

explanation.surface: A woman's dress shows off a wild flower print.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant name is literally a lady's smock; it is also called cuckooflower.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady's smock (cuckooflower) is a pale lilac wildflower of damp meadows.

explanation.surface: A Rolls-Royce owner insists on a final drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A Rolls-Royce is a car, something 'for the road'; the phrase is also a last drink before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rolls is one motor car made for driving; the phrase also names a final drink before travelling.

clue.text: Selfish indulgences, say, ports drunk around Italy

parts.note: e.g., for example, is signalled by say

indicators.note: around says the reworked letters enclose the code for Italy
drunk means reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Downing port wines in Italy is a self-centred treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reworks PORTS into OTRPS, and 'around' puts I inside to give OTRIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego trips are activities done to boost one's own vanity, self-centred pleasures.

indicators.note: surrounded by says the queen's letter is enclosed

parts.note: ensuing means following on
R, for Regina, stands for queen

explanation.surface: The Queen is protected by her retinue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a retinue, but is ENSUING, which takes R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make it certain or secure, a sense of safeguarding.

definitions.meaning: adoption of a cause or belief

explanation.surface: A marriage clinch.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both marriage and the taking up of a cause, as one espouses a belief.

parts.note: sent off, as a missile is discharged

explanation.surface: A railway guard has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guard' suggests a train guard, but is a sentry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch, a guard.

clue.text: Hack's written about page in burst

indicators.note: about means going round, so the cutting word encloses the page letter

parts.note: to slash is to hack or cut

explanation.surface: A journalist's piece concerns a page that's exploded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a journalist, and 'splash' is indeed press slang for a big story, but here it is SLASH round P.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash of colour or water is a sudden burst of it.

clue.text: Brilliance of stone inlaid in charm

indicators.note: inlaid in means set into, as a gem in jewellery

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or charm
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A gem set in a charm bracelet sparkles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone' looks like a gem but is the British weight unit, 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is shine or sheen, a synonym for brilliance.

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the nobleman's title is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's speech is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' says BARON is heard as BARREN.
explanation.definitionFit: Jejune means dull and uninspiring, the figurative sense of barren.

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the word is heard and spelt differently

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling low

explanation.surface: A plant that is said to be blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns LOW into the sound LOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe is a succulent of the lily family, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Flat patch with new rose embedded

indicators.note: embedded means set into, so the remade letters go inside

parts.note: a patch is a period of time, as in a bad patch

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the flower's letters are remade

explanation.surface: A flat garden plot has a fresh rose planted in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a level plot but means dull. 'patch' is a period, as in going through a bad patch; 'new' rearranges the flower inside it to give RESO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome is dull and wearying, as flat is used of lifeless writing.

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: Overall, a committee requires a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on balance' looks like a phrase, but 'on' is a piece and 'balance' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparison weighs one thing against another, as a balance does.

definitions.meaning: a stack of hay or straw

explanation.surface: A haystack built by a little man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rick is a stack of hay; the same letters make a shortened form of the name Richard.
